newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 21.

text.p: THE DOMINION
Mutiny threat over tax cuts: Prime Minister Jim Bolger is facing a mutiny from several high-ranking National MPs over a threat that promised tax cuts will be abandoned. Page 1.
Independent Kopu to break her silence in House: Alamein Kopu has promised to break her silence in Parliament -- by speaking in Maori when the House resumes tomorrow. Page 2.

Treasury aired fears of tax-cut difficulties: The Treasury told the government when the compulsory retirement savings scheme was being designed that matching contributions with tax cuts would be extremely difficult, documents issued at the weekend show. Page 2.

Phillips acquitted on three fraud charges: Former Pacer Kerridge executive chairman David Phillips has been acquitted on three charges of fraud and a retrial was ordered for the remaining four charges he faced. Page 7.
Dairy proposal attracts interest: A multi-million-dollar Asian investor is poised to enter the Southland dairy industry. Page 13.

Removal of trade restriction sought: New Zealand would join the United States, Australia and other countries in seeking consultations with India under the dispute settlement provisions of the World Trade Organisation, International Trade Minister Lockwood Smith has said. Page 13.
THE PRESS

Australia disowns 'loose cannon' report: Australia moved on Sunday to limit the diplomatic fallout from the release of a scathing report which described New Zealand Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters as a "loose cannon" and an opportunist.

Goodman has nearly 60 pct of bread market: New Zealanders have developed an increasing appetite for white bread and pies over the last year, according to the head of New Zealand's biggest bread company.
Carter Holt Harvey buys back forest: Carter Holt Harvey has repurchased about 40,000 hectares of Auckland forest from a group of Japanese investors who have effectively owned them since 1991.

Pacific International quits Tasman run: The Pacific International Lines shipping company is pulling out of the New Zealand-Brisbane run, saying an "orchestrated campaign" by the media, other shipping operators, and the Seafarers' Union has undermined confidence in its service.
Bre-X harmful -- Heritage: The alleged salting of Bre-X's Indonesian prospect has had an adverse impact on Australasian gold shares, says Heritage Gold's chairman, Peter Atkinson.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Govt in the spotlight: Former state-owned enterprises minister Richard Prebble says Clear Communications' action against the government for not enforcing Telecom's undertakings ahead of telecommunications deregulation in 1989 would force the government to state its position on light-handed regulations.
Executives see rates as crucial: A lower exchange rate, lower interest rates and lower taxes are needed to get the economy moving again in the opinion of senior business executives.

Meat players at odds over revamp: The three major forces in the meat industry who agreed on reducing the Meat Board's powers two years ago have acknowledged there are still areas where they are at odds.
Just fine tuning required: John Luxton's Dairy Board restructuring agenda outlined in the Business Herald on Tuesday last week is nothing new.

Ostrich, emu group formed: A group of ostrich and emu industry participants are trying to form a cooperative company to bring together slaughter, processing and marketing operations for the two industries.
Forests put on offer by councils: About 43,000 hectares of Canterbury forests valued at more than $90 million are being offered for development by their councils owners.
